skill.name: adaptyv
skill.description: Guides protein design teams through Adaptyv cloud lab workflows for assay selection, sequence submission, status tracking, result retrieval, and computational pre-screening.
skill.summary: Plan, submit, and track protein validation experiments through Adaptyv workflows.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most high and medium static findings are documentation false positives, including placeholders for API keys, `.env` guidance, Markdown fences, and biological sequence text. The confirmed risk is intentional outbound network access to Adaptyv and related scientific services, which should be disclosed clearly because users may send proprietary protein sequences.

remediation.issue: External API endpoint is hardcoded in examples.
remediation.suggestion: Document the endpoint owner and data handling expectations, and prefer a configurable base URL where practical.

remediation.issue: Examples send protein sequences to external services.
remediation.suggestion: Add a clear warning that proprietary sequences leave the local environment when API examples are run.

remediation.issue: Webhook and result-download examples use placeholder URLs.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to validate webhook endpoints and download URLs before sending sensitive project data.

content.value_statement: Protein teams need a clear path from computational design to wet-lab validation. This skill explains Adaptyv experiment workflows, API usage, result handling, and sequence optimization steps.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to prepare protein sequences for Adaptyv experiment submission.
Provides examples for binding, expression, thermostability, and enzyme activity workflows.
Shows how to authenticate with an Adaptyv API key stored in the environment.
Describes status tracking, webhook usage, result download, and result parsing patterns.
Recommends computational pre-screening tools such as NetSolP, SoluProt, SolubleMPNN, and ESM.
Documents common API endpoints, request fields, response shapes, and error codes.
limitations: Requires separate Adaptyv API access before experiments can be submitted.
Examples depend on external services and may change during the platform alpha or beta period.
Does not perform wet-lab experiments directly inside Claude, Codex, or Claude Code.
Computational predictions are guidance and must be validated experimentally.

use_cases.title: Plan validation for antibody variants
use_cases.description: Choose binding and expression assays, format sequence batches, and prepare metadata for experimental submission.

use_cases.title: Automate experiment tracking
use_cases.description: Use the documented API patterns to submit jobs, monitor status, receive webhook updates, and download completed results.

use_cases.title: Pre-screen sequences before lab work
use_cases.description: Apply solubility, stability, and naturalness checks before selecting candidates for Adaptyv testing.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an experiment type
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a single protein project
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose the right Adaptyv experiment type for these protein design goals: [describe goals]. Explain the required inputs and expected outputs.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a batch submission
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a checklist for submitting these protein variants to Adaptyv as a batch experiment: [paste sequence names and goals]. Include metadata and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design a tracking workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an Adaptyv experiment tracking workflow that uses webhooks when possible and polling only as a fallback. Include result download and parsing steps.

prompt_templates.title: Build an optimization-to-validation plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a full optimization and validation workflow for a protein library. Include NetSolP, SoluProt, SolubleMPNN, ESM, candidate selection, and Adaptyv submission.

output_examples.input: I have 40 antibody variants and need to know which assays to run.
output_examples.output: A concise assay plan that recommends binding and expression testing, lists required sequence and target inputs, and suggests batching related variants together.

output_examples.input: I need to track several Adaptyv experiments after submission.
output_examples.output: A workflow outline covering experiment identifiers, webhook notifications, periodic status checks, result download, and combined result analysis.

output_examples.input: My designed enzyme variants have poor predicted solubility.
output_examples.output: A pre-screening plan that filters with solubility predictors, generates conservative redesigned variants, validates naturalness, and selects candidates for expression testing.

best_practices: Store Adaptyv API keys in environment variables and avoid committing secrets.
Validate FASTA formatting and amino acid characters before submitting experiments.
Use webhooks for long-running experiments instead of frequent polling.
anti_patterns: Submitting every generated sequence without computational filtering or controls.
Hardcoding private API keys in notebooks, scripts, or prompt history.
Treating prediction scores as final evidence without wet-lab validation.

faq.question: Does this skill submit experiments by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow guidance and code examples. Users must run API calls with their own Adaptyv credentials.

faq.question: Which experiment types are covered?
faq.answer: It covers binding assays, expression testing, thermostability testing, enzyme activity assays, and related result workflows.

faq.question: Does it require an API key?
faq.answer: Yes. API examples require an Adaptyv API key stored outside source control, usually in an environment variable.

faq.question: Can it optimize protein sequences?
faq.answer: It describes optimization workflows using external computational tools, then explains how to submit selected candidates for testing.

faq.question: How long do results take?
faq.answer: The referenced documentation states typical Adaptyv results take about 21 days, depending on assay type and project details.

faq.question: Is this suitable for confidential sequences?
faq.answer: Users should review Adaptyv terms and data policies before sending proprietary sequences to any external cloud lab API.
